Executive Management Committee:
Key purpose and responsibilities
The Executive Management Committee played a critical role
in shaping and overseeing the Group’s strategic direction
and operational performance. Its key responsibilities
included:
• Supervising business operations to ensure alignment
with organisational objectives.
• Formulating and executing strategies to enhance
market positioning across business segments.
• Developing policies and procedures to strengthen
internal controls and governance frameworks.
• Monitoring financial performance against approved
strategies and budgets, adjusting as necessary.
• Evaluating strategic and operational plans to drive
business growth and sustainability.
• Ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements,
industry guidelines, and internal policies.
• Overseeing Human Resources Management activities
and Policy implementation.
Assets and Liability Committee:
Key purpose and responsibilities
The Asset & Liability Committee focused on maintaining
financial stability and liquidity. Its key responsibilities
included:
• Developing and implementing liquidity and funding
strategies to meet financial obligations promptly.
• Assessing and mitigating operational risks related to
interest rates, market fluctuations, and exchange rate
movements.
• Evaluating the balance sheet structure and making
recommendations to optimise financial stability.
• Ensuring compliance with statutory requirements on
liquidity, cash reserves, and foreign exchange exposures.
• Reviewing the internal capital adequacy management
program and investment policies to sustain operational
resilience.

Executive Management Committee:
Key purpose and responsibilities
The Management Credit Committee was responsible for
overseeing credit risk management and ensuring prudent
lending practices. Its key responsibilities included:
• Evaluating and approving new credit applications and
renewals within Board-delegated limits.
• Recommending adjustments to credit limits for Board
approval where necessary.
• Ensuring compliance with regulatory guidelines and
credit risk management policies.
• Monitoring and addressing risks that could impact the
quality of the Group’s credit portfolio.
• Reviewing and recommending credit facilities for Board
approval within the established limits.
Assets and Liability Committee:
Key purpose and responsibilities
The Risk Management Sub-Committees played a pivotal
role in identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across
select organisational departments. Their key responsibilities
included:
• Evaluating significant risk factors that could impact
business operations.
• Identifying the sources and potential consequences of
key business risks.
• Assessing the effectiveness of existing policies and
internal controls in managing risks and ensuring
regulatory compliance.
• Overseeing business continuity and disaster recovery
planning to enhance organisational resilience.
• Developing risk mitigation strategies and implementing
corrective measures to address key vulnerabilities.
